proposals_applied_this_week.reasoning: Even setting aside the gap-down case, the missed-signal data shows JUBLFOOD had a 1.4% prior-day move and still fell 5.07%. The threshold of 6.0% is eliminating stocks with modest but real prior-day strength. Halving it to 3.0% would have admitted JUBLFOOD's context without the structural logic_change above, and reduces the risk that the new had_gap_down_spike path needs to do all the heavy lifting. The 10/10 miss rate on this single gate over 30 days is the strongest quantitative signal available in this dataset.
proposals_applied_this_week.expected_impact: Broadens the rally-context qualification to include 2-4% prior-day moves. Combined with the logic_change above, reduces the expected miss rate. Some increase in false positives is possible if stocks with 3-4% prior rallies that are not actually exhausted get through — the downstream spike-candle gates should filter most of these.

structural_proposals.title: Add gap-down-with-spike as a standalone exhaustion context, independent of prior-day rally
structural_proposals.proposed_change: Introduce a new constant EXH_GAP_DOWN_SPIKE_PCT = 2.5. In the exhaustion-context block (currently 'if not (had_rally or had_cumul or had_gap_up)'), add a fourth qualifying path: had_gap_down_spike = (gap_up_pct <= -EXH_GAP_DOWN_SPIKE_PCT) and (c5_move_pct >= EXH_IMPULSE_MOVE_PCT). The idea: a stock that gaps down 2.5%+ and then has a sharp intraday spike candle (the blow-off bounce attempt) is equally valid exhaustion context — the trapped longs from the prior close are the fuel, not prior-day buyers from a rally. The condition should be evaluated at the same point in the gate sequence as had_rally/had_cumul/had_gap_up, so: if not (had_rally or had_cumul or had_gap_up or had_gap_down_spike). The gap_up_pct variable is already computed before this gate; EXH_GAP_DOWN_SPIKE_PCT just needs to be defined at module level alongside the other EXH_ constants.
structural_proposals.reasoning: All 10 of 10 missed signals in the last 30 days were blocked solely by prev_day_rally. Looking at the specific cases: ADANIENT (9.18% fall, actual prev-day rally 0.63%), ADANIPORTS (6.79% fall, 0.09%), ADANIGREEN (6.88% fall, -0.48%), GODREJIND (5.14% fall, -0.1%), JUBLFOOD (5.07% fall, 1.4%) — every one of these had either a flat or negative prior day, suggesting they opened with a gap down or flat and then spiked intraday before reversing hard. The current logic has had_gap_up for positive gaps but no analogous path for a gap-down-then-spike exhaustion structure, which is a distinct and common institutional distribution pattern. The 100% concentration of misses in a single gate (prev_day_rally, gate_blocking_counts shows 10/10) is strong structural evidence that the gate's binary framing is the problem, not its threshold.
structural_proposals.expected_impact: Should recover a meaningful fraction of the 10 missed signals per 30-day window. False-positive risk is bounded because the spike-candle gates (c5_move_pct, c5_turnover, same-slot volume) still apply fully — only the upstream context gate is relaxed for this path. Signal count likely increases by 2-5 per month in gap-down-open sessions.

structural_proposals.title: Add daily RSI minimum gate to require trend alignment before PDH/PDL breakout
structural_proposals.proposed_change: Introduce a new constant MB_RSI_MIN = 55.0 for bullish and implicitly MB_RSI_MAX = 45.0 for bearish (i.e. daily RSI(14) must be below 45 for a bearish Momentum Breakdown signal). Add this gate after the 'opened within yesterday's range' check and before the breakout search loop, using the same _wilder_rsi(daily_closes, 14) computation pattern already present in _screen_pdh_trend. For bullish: if rsi < MB_RSI_MIN, _dbg_fail and continue. For bearish: if rsi > (100 - MB_RSI_MIN), _dbg_fail and continue. The RSI should be computed on daily_closes from the already-loaded daily dataframe, requiring len(daily) >= 16 (add to the existing len(daily) < 2 guard).
structural_proposals.reasoning: Both Momentum directions show 0% win rate with 2 confirmed losses each (not just expirations). The existing logic requires only that the stock opened within the prior day's range — it has no requirement that the stock is actually in a trending condition at the daily level. A PDH break by a stock with daily RSI of 42 (in downtrend territory) is a far weaker setup than the same break with RSI 62. The PDH Breakout panel already uses RSI >= 60 as a gate and is the only panel without a 0% win rate in the momentum category. The Momentum Breakout is a lighter version of PDH Breakout (no EMA200, no VWAP required at screen time), so adding a softer RSI gate (55 vs 60) gives trend alignment without replicating the full PDH screen.
structural_proposals.expected_impact: Reduces signal count by filtering out counter-trend breakout attempts. Expected to improve win rate by ensuring the breakout has daily momentum behind it. May reduce total signals by 30-50% given how broad the current universe scan is without RSI filtering.

structural_proposals.panel: Trap Reversal (Bear Trap Bullish / Bull Trap Bearish)
structural_proposals.title: Flag Trap Reversal panels as statistically unresolved and suppress auto-tuning
structural_proposals.proposed_change: Add a module-level constant TRAP_MIN_SAMPLE_FOR_TUNING = 20. In any auto-tuner or signal-review loop, before proposing parameter changes for the Trap panels, check that the panel's 30-day signal count meets this minimum. This is not a gate change in _screen_trap itself but a meta-guard in the tuning infrastructure. As a related code change, add a panel-level comment in _screen_trap: '# NOTE: sample size < 20 signals over 30 days as of 2026-09-06 — do not tune thresholds off this data.'
structural_proposals.reasoning: Bear Trap Bullish: 7 total signals, 0 wins, 0 losses, 7 expired — no outcome data at all, every signal expired before hitting T1 or SL. Bull Trap Bearish: 2 total signals, both expired. Zero resolved outcomes across 9 combined signals means any apparent 0% win rate is an artefact of the market not moving enough to resolve the trade within session, not evidence of bad signals. Proposing threshold changes off this data would be noise-fitting. The right action is to wait for resolved outcomes before diagnosing.
structural_proposals.expected_impact: No change to live signal quality. Prevents future automated tuning passes from incorrectly treating 'all expired' as a win-rate failure and tightening/loosening gates in response to noise.

structural_proposals.title: Replace fixed Bollinger Band upper gate (referenced in output but bb_upper not computed in visible code) with a relative intraday spike-height gate
structural_proposals.proposed_change: Introduce EXH_SPIKE_HEIGHT_ATR_MIN = 1.5. After the c5_turnover gate and before building the trade plan, compute the prior-day 15-min ATR(10) using the same last_session5 pattern used in ORB: take the prior session's 15-min bars and call _wilder_atr on them with period 10. Then require that the c5 candle's absolute price move (c5_close - c5_open in absolute rupee terms) is >= EXH_SPIKE_HEIGHT_ATR_MIN * atr15_prior. This replaces the intent of the Bollinger upper-band gate (bb_upper appears in the output dict in the visible code but bb_upper is never assigned in the code shown — it would raise a NameError at runtime), while using a volatility-normalised threshold that works across all price levels. Constant name: EXH_SPIKE_HEIGHT_ATR_MIN = 1.5 (the spike must be at least 1.5x the stock's typical 15-min bar size from the prior session).
structural_proposals.reasoning: The existing code references bb_upper in the results.append block ('bb_upper': round(bb_upper, 2)) but bb_upper is never assigned anywhere in the visible _screen_exhaustion_short code — this is a live NameError that would crash the panel for any symbol that passes all prior gates. This is not a threshold question; it is a silent bug. The fix must define bb_upper or replace the gate entirely. Given that all 10 missed signals were blocked before reaching this gate (prev_day_rally blocked them all), it is impossible to know from the available data whether the BB gate itself was responsible for any additional filtering — but the NameError means the BB gate never actually ran, and any stock that passed all other gates would have crashed here. Replacing with an ATR-relative spike height gate achieves the original intent (confirming the spike is 'outside normal') in a more robust and normalised way.
structural_proposals.expected_impact: Fixes a silent NameError that currently prevents any Exhaustion Short signal from ever completing successfully. This alone may be why there are no wins to report for this panel — the panel crashes before appending results. After this fix, the other gate changes become meaningful.
